# Example Org — Authentication & Credential Management Standard

**Document Owner:** IAM Engineering
**Cadence:** Continuous
**Status:** Standard (mandatory)

## 1. Purpose and Scope

This Standard defines the mandatory requirements for authentication, credential management, session control, and system use notification across Example Org information systems. It applies to all organizational users, processes acting on behalf of users, non-organizational users, and devices that connect to Example Org systems, and to all personnel and teams that implement, operate, or audit these capabilities.

IAM Engineering is accountable for this process end to end, including implementation, operation, review, and evidence production. Other teams participate in individual steps as identified below.

## 2. Roles and Responsibilities

- **IAM Engineering** owns this Standard and the authentication and credential management process end to end. IAM Engineering implements, configures, monitors, reviews, and produces the evidence artifacts defined in Section 15.
- **System Owners** determine the elements of the environment that require System Use Notification control, determine how notification compliance will be verified, and provide the periodicity of the check (Section 4.4).
- **Help desk and support personnel** must require user identification for any support transaction that has information security and privacy implications (Section 8.4).
- **Developers and installers of system components** must provide unique authenticators or change default authenticators prior to delivery and installation (Section 10.10).

## 3. Unsuccessful Logon Attempt Controls

### 3.1 Invalid logon attempt limits

Example Org must enforce a limit of [Assignment: organization-defined number] consecutive invalid logon attempts by a user during a [Assignment: organization-defined time period]. ARC-AMPE defines this as five (5) consecutive invalid attempts within a fifteen (15) minute period. [NIST AC-7 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE AC-7 AE Mandatory]

### 3.2 Actions on exceeded attempt limits

When the maximum number of unsuccessful logon attempts is exceeded, Example Org must automatically take one or more of the following actions: lock the account or node for an organization-defined time period (ARC-AMPE: a minimum of thirty (30) minutes); lock the account or node until released by an administrator; delay the next logon prompt per an organization-defined delay algorithm; notify the system administrator; or take another organization-defined action. [NIST AC-7 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE AC-7 AE Mandatory]

### 3.3 Mobile device purge or wipe

Example Org must purge or wipe information from [Assignment: organization-defined mobile devices] based on [Assignment: organization-defined purging or wiping requirements and techniques] after [Assignment: organization-defined number] consecutive, unsuccessful device logon attempts. ARC-AMPE sets this at ten (10) consecutive unsuccessful attempts. [NIST AC-7(2) | ARC-AMPE AC-7(2) AE Mandatory]

### 3.4 Biometric logon attempt limits

Example Org must limit the number of unsuccessful biometric logon attempts to [Assignment: organization-defined number]. [NIST AC-7(3)]

### 3.5 Alternative authentication factors

Example Org must allow the use of [Assignment: organization-defined authentication factors] different from the primary authentication factors after the organization-defined number of consecutive invalid logon attempts has been exceeded, and must enforce a limit of [Assignment: organization-defined number] consecutive invalid logon attempts through use of the alternative factors by a user during a [Assignment: organization-defined time period]. [NIST AC-7(4)]

## 4. System Use Notification

### 4.1 Notification banner

Example Org must display an organization-defined system use notification message or banner to users before granting access to the system that provides privacy and security notices consistent with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines, and states that:

- users are accessing a U.S. Government system (ARC-AMPE wording: a system that contains U.S. Government information);
- system usage may be monitored, recorded, and subject to audit;
- unauthorized use of the system is prohibited and subject to criminal and civil penalties; and
- use of the system indicates consent to monitoring and recording.

[NIST AC-8 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE AC-8 AE Mandatory]

### 4.2 Acknowledgement before access

The notification message or banner must be retained on the screen until users acknowledge the usage conditions and take explicit actions to log on to or further access the system. [NIST AC-8 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE AC-8 AE Mandatory]

### 4.3 Publicly accessible systems

For publicly accessible systems, Example Org must display system use information under [Assignment: organization-defined conditions] before granting further access; must display references, if any, to monitoring, recording, or auditing consistent with the privacy accommodations for such systems (which generally prohibit those activities); and must include a description of the authorized uses of the system. [NIST AC-8 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE AC-8 AE Mandatory]

### 4.4 Verification of notification compliance

The System Owner determines the elements of the environment that require the System Use Notification control, determines how notification compliance will be verified, and provides the periodicity of the check. If verification is not performed as part of a configuration baseline check, a documented agreement covers how verification results are provided and the verification periodicity. [ARC-AMPE AC-8 AE Mandatory]

## 5. Session Control

### 5.1 Concurrent session limits

Example Org must limit the number of concurrent sessions for each [Assignment: organization-defined account and/or account types] to [Assignment: organization-defined number]. [NIST AC-10 High]

Concurrent sessions must be limited for each account and/or account type to one (1) session. A session is an encounter between an end-user interface device (e.g., computer, terminal, process) and an application, including a network logon. Any requirement for more than one (1) concurrent session must be expressly required for the performance of job duties and documented in the applicable security and privacy plan. [ARC-AMPE AC-10 AE Mandatory]

### 5.2 Device lock on inactivity

Example Org must prevent further access to the system by initiating a device lock after a period of inactivity (NIST: [Assignment: organization-defined time period]; ARC-AMPE: fifteen (15) minutes, with inactivity including both remote and internal access connections) and/or by requiring the user to initiate a device lock before leaving the system unattended. ARC-AMPE requires both the timed lock and the user-initiated lock. [NIST AC-11 Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE AC-11 AE Mandatory]

### 5.3 Device lock release

The device lock must be retained until the user reestablishes access using established identification and authentication procedures. [NIST AC-11 Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE AC-11 AE Mandatory]

### 5.4 Concealment of display information

Example Org must conceal, via the device lock, information previously visible on the display with a publicly viewable image. [NIST AC-11(1) Moderate, High]

### 5.5 Automatic session termination

Example Org must automatically terminate a user session after [Assignment: organization-defined conditions or trigger events] (e.g., periods of user inactivity, targeted responses to certain types of incidents, or time-of-day restrictions on system use), including electronic procedures that terminate an electronic session after a predetermined time of inactivity. [NIST AC-12 Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE AC-12 AE Mandatory | HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iii) Addressable]

### 5.6 Logout capability

Example Org must provide a logout capability for user-initiated communications sessions whenever authentication is used to gain access to [Assignment: organization-defined information resources]. ARC-AMPE defines information resources as those defined in the applicable security and privacy plans. [NIST AC-12(1) | ARC-AMPE AC-12(1) AE Mandatory]

### 5.7 Logout message

Example Org must display an explicit logout message to users indicating the termination of authenticated communications sessions. ARC-AMPE requires an organization-defined standard logout message documented in the applicable System Security and Privacy Plan (e.g., "Your session has been terminated"). [NIST AC-12(2) | ARC-AMPE AC-12(2) AE Mandatory]

### 5.8 Session end warning

Example Org must display an explicit message to users indicating that the session will end in [Assignment: organization-defined time]. ARC-AMPE requires that the organization-defined time until end of session be specified in the applicable security and privacy plans. [NIST AC-12(3) | ARC-AMPE AC-12(3) AE Mandatory]

## 6. Workstation Use and Access to Electronic Protected Health Information

### 6.1 Workstation use policies and procedures

Example Org must implement policies and procedures that specify the proper functions to be performed, the manner in which those functions are to be performed, and the physical attributes of the surroundings of a specific workstation or class of workstation that can access electronic protected health information. [HIPAA 164.310(b)]

### 6.2 Access control for systems maintaining ePHI

Example Org must implement technical policies and procedures for electronic information systems that maintain electronic protected health information to allow access only to those persons or software programs that have been granted access rights as specified in § 164.308(a)(4). [HIPAA 164.312(a)(1)]

### 6.3 Emergency access procedures

Example Org must establish (and implement as needed) procedures for obtaining necessary electronic protected health information during an emergency. [HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(ii) Required]

### 6.4 Encryption and decryption of ePHI

Example Org must implement a mechanism to encrypt and decrypt electronic protected health information. [HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv) Addressable]

## 7. Identification and Authentication Policy and Procedures

### 7.1 Policy development and dissemination

IAM Engineering must develop, document, and disseminate to [Assignment: organization-defined personnel or roles] an identification and authentication policy that addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance, and is consistent with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines, together with procedures to facilitate implementation of the policy and associated controls, maintained in written (which may be electronic) form. [NIST IA-1 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE IA-1 AE Mandatory | HIPAA 164.316(b)(1)(i)]

### 7.2 Designated official

Example Org must designate an [Assignment: organization-defined official] to manage the development, documentation, and dissemination of the identification and authentication policy and procedures. [NIST IA-1 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE IA-1 AE Mandatory]

### 7.3 Policy review and update

IAM Engineering must review and update the current identification and authentication policy and procedures [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] and following [Assignment: organization-defined events]. ARC-AMPE requires review at least every one (1) year and following organization-defined events, such as assessment or audit findings, security or privacy incidents, or changes to applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines. Example Org must also review periodically and update as needed in response to environmental or operational changes affecting the security of electronic protected health information. [NIST IA-1 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE IA-1 AE Mandatory | HIPAA 164.316(b)(2)(iii) Required]

### 7.4 Documentation retention

Documentation required under these requirements must be retained for 6 years from the date of its creation or the date when it last was in effect, whichever is later. [HIPAA 164.316(b)(2)(i) Required]

### 7.5 Documentation availability

Documentation must be made available to those persons responsible for implementing the procedures to which the documentation pertains. [HIPAA 164.316(b)(2)(ii) Required]

## 8. Identification and Authentication (Organizational Users)

### 8.1 Unique identification and authentication

Example Org must uniquely identify and authenticate organizational users and processes acting on their behalf, including assigning a unique name and/or number for identifying and tracking user identity, and must verify that a person or entity seeking access to electronic protected health information is the one claimed. [NIST IA-2 Low, Moderate, High | FedRAMP IA-2 | ARC-AMPE IA-2 AE Mandatory | HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(i) Required | HIPAA 164.312(d)]

### 8.2 Identity proofing and authentication processes

Example Org must employ effective identity proofing and authentication processes compliant with the latest published NIST SP 800-63 Digital Identity Guidelines document suite, and must require the use of system and/or network authenticators and unique user identifiers for organizational users. [ARC-AMPE IA-2 AE Mandatory]

### 8.3 Help desk user identification

Example Org must require user identification for any help desk support transaction that has information security and privacy implications. [ARC-AMPE IA-2 AE Mandatory | ARC-AMPE IA-8 AE Mandatory]

### 8.4 Phishing-resistant multi-factor authentication

Multi-factor authentication must be phishing-resistant, in accordance with current CISA guidance. [FedRAMP IA-2 | FedRAMP IA-2(1) | FedRAMP IA-2(2)]

### 8.5 MFA for privileged accounts

Example Org must implement multi-factor authentication for access to privileged accounts, using two or more different factors (something you know, something you have, or something you are) appropriate for the level of risk. [NIST IA-2(1) Low, Moderate, High | FedRAMP IA-2(1) | ARC-AMPE IA-2(1) AE Mandatory]

### 8.6 MFA for non-privileged accounts

Example Org must implement multi-factor authentication for access to non-privileged accounts. ARC-AMPE requires MFA for all non-privileged account types, and strongly recommends (but does not currently mandate) it for consumer accounts. [NIST IA-2(2) Low, Moderate, High | FedRAMP IA-2(2) | ARC-AMPE IA-2(2) AE Mandatory]

### 8.7 Shared accounts and authenticators

When shared accounts or authenticators are employed, Example Org must require users to be individually authenticated before granting access to the shared accounts or resources. [NIST IA-2(5) High | ARC-AMPE IA-2(5) AE Mandatory]

### 8.8 MFA with separate device

Example Org must implement multi-factor authentication for local, network, and remote access to privileged and non-privileged accounts such that (a) one of the factors is provided by a device separate from the system gaining access, and (b) the device meets [Assignment: organization-defined strength of mechanism requirements]. ARC-AMPE requires that the device meets the latest published FIPS 140-compliant cryptography. [NIST IA-2(6) | FedRAMP IA-2(6) | ARC-AMPE IA-2(6) AE Mandatory]

### 8.9 Replay-resistant authentication

Example Org must implement replay-resistant authentication mechanisms for access to privileged and non-privileged accounts. [NIST IA-2(8) Low, Moderate, High | FedRAMP IA-2(8) | ARC-AMPE IA-2(8) AE Mandatory]

### 8.10 Single sign-on

Example Org must provide a single sign-on capability for [Assignment: organization-defined system accounts and services]. [NIST IA-2(10)]

### 8.11 PIV credential acceptance

Example Org must accept and electronically verify Personal Identity Verification-compliant credentials. [NIST IA-2(12) Low, Moderate, High]

### 8.12 Out-of-band authentication

Example Org must implement [Assignment: organization-defined out-of-band authentication] mechanisms under [Assignment: organization-defined conditions]. [NIST IA-2(13)]

## 9. Device Identification and Authentication

### 9.1 Unique device identification and authentication

Example Org must uniquely identify and authenticate [Assignment: organization-defined devices and/or types of devices] before establishing a local, remote, or network connection. ARC-AMPE requires, at a minimum, authentication mechanisms using shared information (MAC or IP address) and access control lists to control remote network access, with the specific devices and/or device types approved for identification and authentication management defined in the applicable System Security and Privacy Plan. [NIST IA-3 Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE IA-3 AE Mandatory]

### 9.2 Cryptographically based bidirectional authentication

Example Org must authenticate [Assignment: organization-defined devices and/or types of devices] before establishing a local, remote, or network connection using bidirectional authentication that is cryptographically based. [NIST IA-3(1)]

### 9.3 Dynamic address allocation

Where addresses are allocated dynamically, Example Org must standardize dynamic address allocation lease information and lease duration assigned to devices in accordance with [Assignment: organization-defined lease information and lease duration], and must audit lease information when assigned to a device. [NIST IA-3(3)]

### 9.4 Attestation-based device authentication

Example Org must handle device identification and authentication based on attestation by [Assignment: organization-defined configuration management process]. [NIST IA-3(4)]

## 10. Authenticator Management

### 10.1 Initial authenticator distribution

IAM Engineering must manage system authenticators by verifying, as part of initial authenticator distribution, the identity of the individual, group, role, service, or device receiving the authenticator, and by establishing initial authenticator content for any authenticators issued by the organization. [NIST IA-5 Low, Moderate, High | FedRAMP IA-5 | ARC-AMPE IA-5 AE Mandatory]

### 10.2 Strength of mechanism

Example Org must ensure that authenticators have sufficient strength of mechanism for their intended use. [NIST IA-5 Low, Moderate, High | FedRAMP IA-5 | ARC-AMPE IA-5 AE Mandatory]

### 10.3 Administrative procedures for authenticator lifecycle

IAM Engineering must establish and implement administrative procedures for initial authenticator distribution, for lost or compromised or damaged authenticators, and for revoking authenticators. [NIST IA-5 Low, Moderate, High | FedRAMP IA-5 | ARC-AMPE IA-5 AE Mandatory]

### 10.4 Default authenticators

Default authenticators must be changed prior to first use. [NIST IA-5 Low, Moderate, High | FedRAMP IA-5 | ARC-AMPE IA-5 AE Mandatory]

### 10.5 Authenticator change and refresh

Authenticators must be changed or refreshed [Assignment: organization-defined time period by authenticator type] or when [Assignment: organization-defined events] occur. ARC-AMPE requires immediate change when authenticators are no longer valid due to known or suspected compromise, and immediate change upon system installation (e.g., default or vendor-supplied passwords), and strongly recommends changing organizational System/User Account passwords at least once every six (6) months. [NIST IA-5 Low, Moderate, High | FedRAMP IA-5 | ARC-AMPE IA-5 AE Mandatory]

### 10.6 Protection of authenticator content

Example Org must protect authenticator content from unauthorized disclosure and modification, and must require individuals to take, and have devices implement, specific controls to protect authenticators (e.g., maintaining possession, not sharing authenticators, and immediately reporting lost, stolen, or compromised authenticators). [NIST IA-5 Low, Moderate, High | FedRAMP IA-5 | ARC-AMPE IA-5 AE Mandatory]

### 10.7 Group and role account authenticators

Authenticators for group or role accounts must be changed when membership to those accounts changes. [NIST IA-5 Low, Moderate, High | FedRAMP IA-5 | ARC-AMPE IA-5 AE Mandatory]

### 10.8 NIST SP 800-63B compliance and MFA pairing

Example Org must comply with the latest published NIST SP 800-63B for authenticator management. Organizational System/User Account passwords must be paired with multi-factor authentication (MFA) solutions, and MFA is strongly recommended for ACA Consumer Account passwords. [ARC-AMPE IA-5 AE Mandatory]

### 10.9 Authenticator assurance levels

Authenticators must be compliant with the most recent NIST Digital Identity Guidelines IAL, AAL, and FAL levels appropriate to the certification class: Class B requires level 1, Class C requires level 2, and Class D requires level 3. [FedRAMP IA-5]

### 10.10 Developer and installer authenticator requirements

Example Org must require developers and installers of system components to provide unique authenticators or change default authenticators prior to delivery and installation. [NIST IA-5(5)]

### 10.11 Protection commensurate with information security category

Example Org must protect authenticators commensurate with the security category of the information to which use of the authenticator permits access. [NIST IA-5(6) Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE IA-5(6) AE Mandatory]

### 10.12 No embedded static authenticators

Example Org must ensure that unencrypted static authenticators are not embedded in applications or other forms of static storage. [NIST IA-5(7) | ARC-AMPE IA-5(7) AE Mandatory]

### 10.13 Multiple-system account risk

Example Org must implement [Assignment: organization-defined security controls] to manage the risk of compromise due to individuals having accounts on multiple systems. [NIST IA-5(8)]

### 10.14 Federated credentials

Example Org must use [Assignment: organization-defined external organizations] to federate credentials. [NIST IA-5(9)]

### 10.15 Dynamic binding of identities and authenticators

Example Org must bind identities and authenticators dynamically using [Assignment: organization-defined binding rules]. [NIST IA-5(10)]

### 10.16 Biometric quality requirements

For biometric-based authentication, Example Org must employ mechanisms that satisfy [Assignment: organization-defined biometric quality requirements]. [NIST IA-5(12)]

### 10.17 Cached authenticators

Example Org must prohibit the use of cached authenticators after [Assignment: organization-defined time period]. [NIST IA-5(13)]

### 10.18 PKI trust store management

For PKI-based authentication, Example Org must employ an organization-wide methodology for managing the content of PKI trust stores installed across all platforms, including networks, operating systems, browsers, and applications. [NIST IA-5(14)]

### 10.19 GSA-approved ICAM products and services

Example Org must use only General Services Administration-approved products and services for identity, credential, and access management. [NIST IA-5(15) | ARC-AMPE IA-8(2) AE Mandatory]

### 10.20 Authenticator issuance

Example Org must require that the issuance of [Assignment: organization-defined types of and/or specific authenticators] be conducted [Selection: in person; by a trusted external party] before [Assignment: organization-defined registration authority] with authorization by [Assignment: organization-defined personnel or roles]. [NIST IA-5(16)]

### 10.21 Presentation attack detection

Example Org must employ presentation attack detection mechanisms for biometric-based authentication. [NIST IA-5(17)]

### 10.22 Password managers

Example Org must employ [Assignment: organization-defined password managers] to generate and manage passwords, and must protect the passwords using [Assignment: organization-defined controls]. [NIST IA-5(18)]

## 11. Password Requirements

### 11.1 Compromised password list

IAM Engineering must maintain a list of commonly-used, expected, or compromised passwords and must update the list [Assignment: organization-defined frequency]. ARC-AMPE requires a frequency defined in applicable security/privacy plans, not to exceed one (1) year, and requires updates when organizational passwords are suspected to have been compromised directly or indirectly. [NIST IA-5(1) Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE IA-5(1) AE Mandatory]

### 11.2 Password verification against list

When users create or update passwords, Example Org must verify that the passwords are not found on the list of commonly-used, expected, or compromised passwords. [NIST IA-5(1) Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE IA-5(1) AE Mandatory]

### 11.3 Cryptographically protected transmission

Passwords must be transmitted only over cryptographically protected channels. [NIST IA-5(1) Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE IA-5(1) AE Mandatory]

### 11.4 Salted key derivation storage

Passwords must be stored using an approved salted key derivation function, preferably using a keyed hash. [NIST IA-5(1) Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE IA-5(1) AE Mandatory]

### 11.5 Password change upon account recovery

Example Org must require immediate selection of a new password upon account recovery. [NIST IA-5(1) Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE IA-5(1) AE Mandatory]

### 11.6 Long passwords and passphrases

Example Org must allow user selection of long passwords and passphrases, including spaces and all printable characters. [NIST IA-5(1) Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE IA-5(1) AE Mandatory]

### 11.7 Automated password assistance

Example Org must employ automated tools to assist the user in selecting strong password authenticators. [NIST IA-5(1) Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE IA-5(1) AE Mandatory]

### 11.8 Composition and complexity rules

Example Org must enforce [Assignment: organization-defined composition and complexity rules] for passwords. ARC-AMPE requires compliance with the latest published NIST SP 800-63B, with a minimum of eight (8) characters for ACA Consumer Accounts, a minimum of twelve (12) characters for Administrator/Privileged Accounts, and a minimum of eight (8) characters for all other accounts. [NIST IA-5(1) Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE IA-5(1) AE Mandatory]

## 12. Public Key and PKI Authentication

### 12.1 Private key protection and identity mapping

For public key-based authentication, Example Org must enforce authorized access to the corresponding private key, and must map the authenticated identity to the account of the individual or group. [NIST IA-5(2) Moderate, High]

### 12.2 Certificate validation

When public key infrastructure (PKI) is used, Example Org must validate certificates by constructing and verifying a certification path to an accepted trust anchor, including checking certificate status information, and must implement a local cache of revocation data to support path discovery and validation. [NIST IA-5(2) Moderate, High]

### 12.3 Encrypted authentication assertions

Example Org must encrypt authentication assertions when passed through third parties, such as a browser (e.g., a SAML assertion encrypted using XML-Encryption, or an OpenID Connect ID Token encrypted using JSON Web Encryption). [FedRAMP IA-5]

## 13. Authentication Feedback and Cryptographic Module Authentication

### 13.1 Obscured authentication feedback

Example Org must obscure feedback of authentication information during the authentication process to protect the information from possible exploitation and use by unauthorized individuals. [NIST IA-6 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE IA-6 AE Mandatory]

### 13.2 Cryptographic module authentication

Example Org must implement mechanisms for authentication to a cryptographic module that meet the requirements of applicable laws, executive orders, directives, policies, regulations, standards, and guidelines for such authentication. [NIST IA-7 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE IA-7 AE Mandatory]

### 13.3 FIPS 140-compliant encryption for PII systems

Example Org must use the latest published FIPS 140-compliant encryption standards for information systems containing Personally Identifiable Information (PII). [ARC-AMPE IA-7 AE Mandatory]

## 14. Non-Organizational Users

### 14.1 Unique identification and authentication

Example Org must uniquely identify and authenticate non-organizational users or processes acting on behalf of non-organizational users. [NIST IA-8 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE IA-8 AE Mandatory]

### 14.2 Identity proofing for non-organizational users

Example Org must employ effective identity proofing and authentication processes compliant with the latest published NIST SP 800-63 Digital Identity Guidelines document suite (ARC-AMPE: compliant with NIST SP 800-63-3 IAL-2/AAL-2), and must require the use of system and/or network authenticators and unique user identifiers for non-organizational users. [ARC-AMPE IA-8 AE Mandatory]

### 14.3 PIV credentials from other federal agencies

Example Org must accept and electronically verify Personal Identity Verification-compliant credentials from other federal agencies. [NIST IA-8(1) Low, Moderate, High]

### 14.4 External authenticator acceptance

Example Org must accept only external authenticators that are NIST-compliant, and must document and maintain a list of accepted external authenticators. ARC-AMPE additionally requires that external credentials be certified as compliant with the latest published NIST SP 800-63 Digital Identity Guidelines by an approved accreditation authority, meet or exceed those guidelines, and that the organization use GSA-approved products and services for identity, credential, and access management. [NIST IA-8(2) Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE IA-8(2) AE Mandatory]

### 14.5 Identity management profiles

Example Org must conform to [Assignment: organization-defined identity management profiles], defined using identity proofing and authentication processes compliant with the latest published NIST SP 800-63 Digital Identity Guidelines document suite. [NIST IA-8(4) Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE IA-8(4) AE Mandatory]

### 14.6 Federated and PKI credential acceptance

Example Org must accept and verify federated or PKI credentials that meet [Assignment: organization-defined policy]. [NIST IA-8(5)]

### 14.7 Disassociation of user attributes

Example Org must implement [Assignment: organization-defined measures] to disassociate user attributes or identifier assertion relationships among individuals, credential service providers, and relying parties. [NIST IA-8(6)]

## 15. Re-authentication

Example Org must require users to re-authenticate when [Assignment: organization-defined circumstances or situations] occur, such as when authenticators, roles, or credentials change, when security categories of systems change, when execution of privileged functions occurs, or after a fixed time period. ARC-AMPE requires that circumstances requiring re-authentication be defined in the applicable security/privacy plans, including at a minimum after a fixed time period. [NIST IA-11 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE IA-11 AE Mandatory]

## 16. Evidence and Records

IAM Engineering produces and retains the following evidence artifacts in support of this Standard, on a continuous basis:

- **MFA enrolment report** — generated and retained by IAM Engineering as evidence of multi-factor authentication enrolment for privileged and non-privileged accounts (Sections 8.5 and 8.6).
- **Authentication policy configuration export** — generated and retained by IAM Engineering as evidence of the enforced authentication policy configuration, including logon attempt limits, device lock settings, session controls, and password rules (Sections 3, 5, and 11).

Documentation required under this Standard is retained in accordance with Section 7.4 and made available in accordance with Section 7.5.
